newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia forex reserves seen at $20 bln in 97/98.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia forex reserves seen at $20 bln in 97/98.

text.p: Central bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono said on Monday Indonesia's foreign exchange reserves were expected to rise to $20 billion in the 1997/98 (April-March) fiscal year.

Djiwandono said the country's foreign exchange reserves were estimated to rise in the next fiscal year starting April 1 on the back of capital inflows forecast at $10.8 billion against an estimated current account deficit of $9.8 billion.

He told a briefing ahead of President Suharto's 1997/98 budget address to parliament on Monday that foreign exchange reserves in the current fiscal year ending March 31 were expected to reach $19.1 billion, equivalent to some 4.7 or 4.8 months of imports.
Djiwandono said capital inflows to Indonesia were more longer-term than short-term.
He said only five percent of capital inflows were less than one year, 26 percent were between one and three years, with the remaining staying in the country for more than three years.
